data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The advantage of a bounded harness is purely statistical (Extreme Value Theory): it increases the number of independent samples (N), making the maximum quality of the set strictly greater than a single sample, regardless of the 'selection' logic quality.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the model outputs are highly autocorrelated (lack of diversity) across calls, increasing N yields diminishing returns.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the cost of generation scales linearly with N but quality gains are logarithmic, the efficiency ratio favors a single, highly optimized call.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the harness actively modifies the generation context (non-independent samples), the statistical independence assumption fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Sampling Volume: Even a 'dumb' harness that generates N variations and picks the least-worst one outperforms a single call simply because P(max(Q_1...Q_N) > Q_single) approaches 1 as N increases, assuming non-zero probability of a good output. The 'survival' is just observing the tail of the distribution.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
